recommendation: Keep the source-changing commit as-is. It completes the published FHIR-32467 application in current core source without reopening the already-applied StructureDefinition changes.
issue_request: FHIR-32467 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested removal of AuditEvent.entity.type as redundant with AuditEvent.entity.what, with the DICOM mapping updated to preserve ParticipantObjectTypeCode semantics.
initial_application: Commit 1495aa7007 removed AuditEvent.entity.type from the AuditEvent StructureDefinition and moved ParticipantObjectTypeCode into the AuditEvent.entity.what DICOM mapping. Later cleanup removed another entity.type reference from the entity.query comment, but the AuditEvent notes page still contained OperationOutcome guidance for the deleted element.
additional_context: AuditEvent is active in source/fhir.ini, and the Security WG September 2021 block vote listed FHIR-32467 as Persuasive. Current authoritative AuditEvent structure source has no entity.type element, so the remaining notes text was stale rather than a later specification decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/auditevent/auditevent-notes.xml so the OperationOutcome note says entity.what is a reference to the OperationOutcome and removed the obsolete entity.type paragraph. The existing StructureDefinition already contains the element removal and DICOM mapping, so no conformance-source change was needed.
source_changes: source/auditevent/auditevent-notes.xml: clarified that entity.what is a reference to the OperationOutcome and removed the paragraph instructing use of deleted entity.type.

related_jiras.note: Another AuditEvent.entity.type tracker in the same Security WG block vote; it was background only because this reconciliation is scoped to FHIR-32467's redundant element removal.
Later AuditEvent.patient work removed a separate patient-subject narrative that had also mentioned entity.type, leaving the OperationOutcome note as the remaining stale reference.
